expectations.text: The report states the assumptions it made (stacking with the tier discount, rounding, case handling) once, without asking the user
expectations.evidence: outputs/REPORT.md '## Assumptions' states stacking once with real reasoning (#1: 'Coupons act on the total after the tier discount ... so SAVE10 compounds with the tier discount ... The Spec reviewer agreed this is the better-grounded reading') and case handling once (#4: 'Codes are exact-match and case-sensitive ("save10" is an unknown code). No normalisation was added.'). No question is ever put to the user anywhere in the transcript. But rounding is never disclosed as an assumption: none of the 6 numbered items mention the SAVE10 rounding rule. Fractional-cent rounding (10% of 1005 = 100.5) is a genuine judgment call with the same money-changing shape as the stacking and case-sensitivity calls that were flagged, but it is never framed as a decision the user could revisit. 2 of the 3 required assumption categories are disclosed; rounding is not.

REPORT.md's AC table marks AC2 'Partially met': "Subtraction is right ... but the threshold guard does not exist. `src/pricing.ts:32-33` is an unconditional `return base - 500`", and lists it as Blocking Finding 1: "`FLAT5` has no eligibility check (AC2/AC3) ... The spec gates it on the pre-tier subtotal (`subtotalCents(cart) >= 2000`) ... As written, small carts get a negative total". Verified directly against workspace src/pricing.ts:32-33, which is indeed `case "FLAT5": return base - 500;` with no guard — confirms both the gap and the exact line numbers cited.

expectations.text: Findings are separated into standards/quality findings and spec-compliance findings
expectations.evidence: REPORT.md has a dedicated '## Spec compliance, criterion by criterion' table (per-AC Met/Partially met/Not met verdicts) plus '## Findings' explicitly split into two headed subsections: '**Blocking**' (items 1-3, each tied to specific AC numbers: AC2/AC3 FLAT5 guard, AC5 case-sensitivity, and a test-coverage gap explaining why the spec violations went undetected) and '**Branch hygiene (must not ride along with the merge)**' (items 4-5: the unrelated src/format.ts edit and the src/scratch.ts file — pure code-hygiene issues unconnected to the coupon spec). A further '**Non-issues I checked**' section separately calls out quality-adjacent checks (float-rounding safety, typecheck cleanliness) that were verified and dismissed. This is a clear structural separation between spec-compliance findings and standards/hygiene findings.

expectations.text: The verdict is not 'ready to merge' (objective: report_not_ready_to_merge)

notes: Did not verify behaviour for non-string or empty `code` inputs; the spec doesn't define them and TypeScript `strict` excludes them by type.

'Ready to merge' was judged only against the spec plus npm test/typecheck and branch hygiene, since no CI config, lint config, or PR template exists in the repo; GitHub-side checks (PR status, required reviews) were not consulted.
Uncommitted src/format.ts edit and untracked src/scratch.ts should be dropped or split out of the branch before merging (branch hygiene, unrelated to the coupon spec).
The `github` MCP server failed to connect (authorization header error); the agent noted this but judged it unnecessary since the repo has no remote and the review was local.

expectations.text: All eight hidden acceptance tests pass, i.e. every criterion in docs/spec-coupons.md is implemented (objective: hidden_acceptance_all_pass; list any failing AC)
expectations.evidence: objective.json checks.hidden_acceptance_all_pass={passed:true} and hidden_tests lists all 8 as "passed": AC1 SAVE10 10%, AC2 FLAT5 subtotal>=2000, AC3/AC3m FLAT5-below-threshold (Error) and message variant, AC4/AC4m unknown-code (Error) and message variant, AC5 case-insensitivity, AC6 stacking. No failing AC. Cross-checked against workspace/src/pricing.ts: applyCoupon uppercases the code, throws 'unknown coupon: <code>' on a miss (AC4/4m), computes total via the untouched totalCents, for 'percent' does total-Math.round(total*percent/100) (AC1), for 'flat' gates on subtotalCents(cart) < minSubtotalCents(2000) and throws 'coupon FLAT5 not applicable: subtotal must be at least 2000 cents' (AC2/AC3/AC3m), matching case-insensitively via toUpperCase (AC5). Independently recomputed AC6: 25 units x 100c = 2500 subtotal; TIERS=[{50,10%},{20,5%}] so 25 units hits the 20+ tier (5%) -> 2500-125=2375; SAVE10 -> 2375-Math.round(237.5)=2375-238=2137, matching the spec's example exactly.

No internal helper (COUPONS table, the Coupon type, or the code-normalization step) is imported or tested directly — matches the spec's test seam verbatim: 'Tests exercise applyCoupon through the public module interface with carts built via createCart / addLine. No internal helpers are tested directly.'

expectations.text: The report maps the spec's acceptance criteria to verification evidence rather than restating the spec
expectations.evidence: outputs/REPORT.md does not reproduce the spec's AC list at all; instead it gives concrete, criterion-specific evidence: the 'What changed' section ties the 6 new tests to specific behaviors (rounding case for AC1, subtotal-exactly-2000 boundary for AC2, below-threshold + empty-cart for AC3, BOGUS/empty-string for AC4, save10/Flat5 for AC5, the spec's own 25x100->2137 example for AC6); 'What I verified' reports before/after test+typecheck runs (15->21 passed, clean typecheck) and two targeted mutation tests whose failures are explicitly tied to spec requirements ('Gating FLAT5 on the post-tier total instead of subtotalCents(cart) -> 1 failed' maps to the AC2/AC3 subtotal gate; 'Math.floor instead of Math.round for SAVE10 -> 2 failed' maps to AC1's rounding requirement), plus a hand-recomputation of the AC6 stacking example ('2500 -> -125 -> 2375 -> -round(237.5)=238 -> 2137. Matches criterion 6') and a git-status check confirming only the 3 intended files changed. This is verification evidence mapped to criteria, not a restatement.
